name: Battle of Iwo Jima

phases.title: The Marines land on the southeastern coast
phases.text: The first wave of Marines landed on the southeastern beaches, the 5th Marine Division in the southern sector and the 4th in the northern. The beach soon became congested with men and materiel on the loose volcanic ash.

phases.title: The Japanese open fire on the crowded beach
phases.text: The Japanese held their fire for just over an hour while the Americans crowded the beach, then opened fire from their fortified positions on the landing force.

phases.title: The 28th Marines cross the island; the 25th hit the Quarry
phases.text: On the left the 28th Marines drove across the island at its narrowest point and cut off the Japanese on Mount Suribachi. On the right the 25th Marines attacked the Quarry in two prongs against heavy fire.

phases.title: Mount Suribachi is cut off and the flag goes up
phases.text: The 28th Marines turned against the mountain. A patrol from E Company, 2nd Battalion, climbed the volcano and raised a flag at the top. Most of the Japanese there stayed in the tunnels and were generally killed.

phases.title: The 9th Marines attack at night towards Hill 362
phases.text: In the north the fighting bogged down against positions the Japanese reoccupied through their tunnels. Erskine sent the 9th Marines forward in the dark, without a barrage, which helped take Hill 362.

phases.title: The Japanese counterattack for Hill 362
phases.text: The local Japanese commander, against Kuribayashi's order, led a banzai charge of about 1,000 men to retake the hill. The Marines counted 784 Japanese dead the next day.

phases.title: The 3rd Marine Division reaches the northern coast
phases.text: On the same day elements of the 3rd Marine Division reached the northern coast and split the Japanese defence in two. The plan stops drawing Inouye's force after its charge.

phases.title: The 5th Marine Division faces the northern gorge
phases.text: The 5th Marine Division still faced the main stronghold in a gorge at the northwestern end of the island. On 21 March the Marines destroyed the command post there with explosives, and on 24 March they sealed the remaining caves at the northern tip.

phases.title: The last Japanese counterattack
phases.text: After the island was declared secure, a 300-man Japanese force attacked near Airfield No. 2. Army pilots, Seabees and Marines fought it for up to 90 minutes. The island was officially declared secure at 09:00 on 26 March.

note: This plan shows the five weeks of the operation on the whole island, not a single field. The island is drawn as a simple strip with the landing beaches on its eastern side; the accounts give the sectors and the order of events but not exact positions, so the places of the hills, the airfield and the Quarry are schematic.
